prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct GcdCalculator and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: gcd(12, 18) -> 6 is the example in every textbook and it passes two of these three broken implementations. The sign bug only appears when the NEGATIVE argument is the second one -- gcd(-12, 18) happens to come out right and gcd(12, -18) does not, so a checker that tries only one arrangement of the minus sign certifies it. The zero cases are the other half: they are stated explicitly in the contract precisely because they are where a division by zero lives, and a test suite that never passes 0 will never find it.
hints: Try the negative on BOTH sides: gcd(-12, 18) and gcd(12, -18). One of those two passes for a buggy implementation and the other does not.
The contract spells out gcd(0, 5), gcd(5, 0) and gcd(0, 0). Those are stated separately because that is where a % b divides by zero.
Include a pair where one number divides the other exactly, like gcd(6, 3) -> 3: an implementation that starts its search below the smaller number misses it.
